rationale: M49/M37 #866: a FIELD member declared inside an anonymous class body (new Runnable() { int field = target() }) is a symbol owned by the ANONYMOUS type, and the call made from its initialiser is attributed to that type. groovy already honoured this (measured alongside java in script/m14/tmp/anon-member-symbol-census.ts); the fixture pins it so the family contract is stated by every language that satisfies it. The `local` control pins the OTHER half of the same boundary: a method-local is not a project symbol. Call lines are pinned because the `local` call in build() is legitimately attributed to build.

expectSymbols.name: field
expectSymbols.comment: #866 contract 1: the anon body's field is a symbol owned by the anon type

forbidSymbols.name: local
forbidSymbols.comment: #866 control: a method-local is not a project symbol

expectRelationships.comment: #866 contract 2: the initialiser call belongs to the anon type, at the call's own line
control: the method-LOCAL's call IS attributed to build

forbidRelationships.comment: the field initialiser's call must NOT flatten onto the enclosing method
JD18 leak direction: members of an anonymous body never attribute to the enclosing type
